text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in canary-ramp cluster for model 'redwood-v5' (streaming). Threshold breach: p99 > 2.5s across 3 consecutive 1-min buckets. Autoscale healthy. Paging oncall: @Anya

Anya: oncall here, looking now. which canary shard? any rollout id?

DeployBot: rollout started 1749001000 by kevin. version: redwood-v5 commit: 4f3a2b1. canary traffic = 12% globally.

Sam: seeing streaming stalls in logs, lots of `kv_cache` eviction warnings. p95 ~ 800ms but p99 ~ 3.6s and streaming stalls (clients seeing partial chunks then big gap).

Marta: grabbing query patterns in case it's input distribution. prom query: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_inference_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))` — shows tail at encoder step.

Anya: ok, potential causes: (1) kernel regression in v5, (2) changed tokenizer causing longer seqs, (3) cache pressure. Any customer-facing errors?

Customer Success: got 3 reports in the last 5m: streaming pauses, one timed out at 30s. customers: tx-analytics, docbot, sales-assistant. They flagged timeouts.

Kevin: I rolled forward quant changes in v5 to improve perf. metric checks passed in staging. Oncall, I can reduce canary to 0% if we agree.

Luis: quick triage steps: (A) throttle canary traffic to 0-1% (B) rollback to v4 (C) disable streaming on v5 (D) increase KV cache size on hosts. Which first?

Anya: we need live mitigation that is lowest risk -> throttle to 1% first to limit exposure while we validate. If that doesn't drop p99 quickly, rollback.

Sam: running a quick grep on node logs shows repeated `kv_cache: evict miss` lines every ~200ms on hosts serving v5. memory usage + swap negligible. suspect different KV eviction pattern.

Marta: also noticed median input length for canary is up 20% (from user payloads). could be triggering different attention kernel.

Anya: action: Kevin please throttle canary to 1%. Kevin: can you run routing change? use internal admin API or k8s?

Kevin: doing admin route change now. command:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/traffic/shift" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"model":"redwood-v5","percent":1}'
```Applying...

DeployBot: traffic shift api accepted, change id: shift-1749001250, propagation started.

Anya: monitoring p99 / streaming errors. Sam keep watching logs, Marta check seq length distribution on canary.

Sam: logs: after throttle started (≈1749001260) stall rate dropped ~35% but p99 still at ~2.1s. Not back to normal yet.

Marta: seq length for v5 canary still +18% compared to baseline. could explain residual tail.

Luis: given partial improvement but still above SLO (p99 target 1s), recommend rollback to v4 for canary traffic. rollback should be fast and low risk.

Anya: agree. Kevin, please initiate rollback of canary to redwood-v4 for 0-12% window. Prefer full rollback of canary variant.

Kevin: initiating rollback now. command:```bash
# rollback canary v5 -> v4
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal.redwood/api/v1/rollouts/rollback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"rollout_id":"1749001000","target_version":"redwood-v4"}'
```

DeployBot: rollback accepted, rollout 1749001000 -> rollback in progress, expected propagation ~90s.

Sam: post-rollback metrics (1749001360): p99 dropped to 980ms, p95 420ms. streaming stall logs nearly gone.

Anya: nice, we are back under SLO. :thumbsup: Confirmed no new timeouts from customers in last 10m. Customer Success please follow up with affected customers and offer incident note.

Customer Success: will open support threads and send post-incident email. will include timeline, mitigation (rollback), and ask for logs from tx-analytics for root-cause follow-up.

Kevin: safe to keep v5 paused in canary. I'll open a follow-up PR to revert quant changes and run more perf tests on longer sequences.

Marta: for RCA: need to compare kv eviction traces between v4/v5, tokenizer output lengths, and kernel selection logs. I'll start an eval run with synthetic longer sequences.

Anya: Questions for follow-up: - Is this strictly v5 regression on attention kernels? - Did canary traffic pattern differ? - Were autoscaling thresholds masking underlying perf issue? Put owners on each.

Luis: tagging owners: Kevin -> deployment/rollouts, Marta -> perf/evals, Sam -> runtime logs & kv cache, Anya -> incident owner.

Anya: we'll keep this thread as the incident record. Next steps: 1) Kevin to keep v5 paused, 2) Marta perf run results in next 6h, 3) Sam upload logs to incident bucket, 4) CS complete customer contact. Handoff to next oncall in 2h.

DeployBot: incident note created: INC-1749001234, severity: P2, status: mitigated (rollback).

Anya: thanks team — closing paging but leaving thread open for RCA.

Kevin: thanks all. ping me if you need the rollback artifacts.

Sam: uploading logs to s3://incidents/1749001234/logs.tar.gz now.

Marta: starting synthetic suite, will post results here.

Customer Success: first customer outreach drafts in #customer-updates, will post here when sent.
